subparts.author_conclusion: The remainder is zero or has degree strictly less than the divisor degree n.
subparts.author_derivation: For a reduced polynomial division,if a nonzero remainderRhad degree at leastn,its leading term could be cancelled by subtracting a suitable multiple of the divisor. Adding that multiple to the quotient gives a lower-degree remainder,so the previous expression was not reduced. Constant divisors leave remainder0. Thus degR<nfor nonzeroR; the zero case is allowed. This independently derives the statement in the printed key.
subparts.method: Author algebraic proof using leading-term cancellation and the definition of reduced polynomial division; compared with the actual key sentence. Not mechanically proved.
